name: jsonata

parameters.name: expression
parameters.description: A [JSONata expression](https://docs.jsonata.org/expressions). Typically a SQL literal — when it's constant the extension parses it once and reuses the compiled program across every row.

parameters.name: json_data
parameters.description: The JSON value the expression is evaluated against. Any DuckDB [`JSON`](https://duckdb.org/docs/data/json/json_functions.html) value — column, literal, or function result.

parameters.name: bindings
parameters.description: Optional. JSON object whose keys become `$variable` names accessible inside the expression. Use it to parameterize a static expression with per-query values (thresholds, ids, dates).

returns: Result of evaluating the expression — typed as [`JSON`](https://duckdb.org/docs/data/json/json_functions.html). Cast (`::VARCHAR`, `::DOUBLE`, `::JSON[]`) or `unnest` downstream depending on what the expression returns.
description:
Evaluates a JSONata expression against a JSON document and returns the result as `JSON`.

JSONata is a lightweight query and transformation language for JSON, modelled on XPath. The expression can be a path traversal, an array predicate filter, an object-construction literal that reshapes the input, or any combination — all in one string.

Two arities:

- `jsonata(expression, json_data)` — the common form.
- `jsonata(expression, json_data, bindings)` — passes a `bindings` JSON object whose keys become `$variable` names inside the expression. Useful when the expression is a SQL constant but the parameters are per-query (e.g. a threshold lifted from a SQL variable).

When `expression` is a SQL constant — the typical case — it's parsed once per thread and the compiled program is reused per row. Per-row cost is JSON walk + apply.

In the DuckDB 2.0 build each evaluation is bounded by `jsonata_timeout_ms` (default 10 seconds) and `jsonata_max_depth` (default 1000), stops when the query is cancelled, and regular expressions use RE2 (no lookaround or backreferences). Expressions that call `$now()`, `$millis()` or `$random()` are evaluated for every row.

An expression that matches nothing returns the JSON value `null`, not SQL `NULL`; a SQL `NULL` expression or document returns SQL `NULL`. An expression that fails to parse raises `Invalid Input Error: Invalid JSONata expression: …`.

The full JSONata language reference, including string functions, numeric functions, aggregation, higher-order functions, sorting and grouping, and programming constructs, applies. The interactive JSONata exerciser is the fastest way to iterate on an expression before pasting it into SQL.

Filter an array with a predicate, then project

name: jsonata_validate

parameters.name: expression
parameters.description: A string to check as a [JSONata expression](https://docs.jsonata.org/expressions).

returns: `true` if the string parses as a JSONata expression, `false` if it does not, and `NULL` for `NULL` input.
description:
Checks whether a string is a syntactically valid JSONata expression, without evaluating it. New in the DuckDB 2.0 build.

Use it to vet expressions stored in a table before running them with [`jsonata`](#jsonata), or to filter out the bad ones. Validation only parses: an expression that is valid syntax but fails at run time (an unknown function, a type error, runaway recursion) still returns `true`. Regular expressions are compiled as part of parsing, so a pattern that RE2 rejects (lookaround, backreferences) makes the expression invalid.

examples.code:
SELECT jsonata_validate('Account.Order[0].Product') AS ok,
       jsonata_validate('$sum(') AS broken;

examples.description: Only evaluate the stored expressions that parse
